title: CLAUDE.md said a source-touching PR fires source-gates twice; the path filter is per-PUSH, so the head commit decides and the handoff built on it would have waited forever
description:
Found while following a predecessor handoff, not by auditing the file.

THE HANDOFF SAID, as step 1 of an ordered list: "gh pr checks 145 -- wait for both source-gates runs (a source-touching PR fires it twice here, pull_request + push; that is correct, not a duplicate)". That instruction is a faithful application of this repository CLAUDE.md profile section, whose heading read "A source-touching PR fires source-gates twice; a .quest/-only one fires it once".

PR #145 touched src/application/agents/guides.ts and a test file, so it is source-touching by that wording. Its head SHA 4374c69 carried ONE source-gates row, and mergeStateStatus was already CLEAN. A successor following the instruction waits forever for a second run that correctly never existed.

THE MECHANISM, measured rather than reasoned. The push trigger in .github/workflows/prepublication-qualification.yml is path-filtered (src/**, test/**, bin/**, npm/**, scripts/qualification/**, package.json, bun.lock, tsconfig.json, four named scripts) and the filter applies to EACH INDIVIDUAL PUSH, never to the pull request cumulative diff. The pull_request trigger has no path filter at all, which is why exactly one row always appears.

Across the three heads of PR #145:
  200f203  src/ + test/    push run fired      source-gates x2
  cbea37e  test/           push run fired      source-gates x2
  4374c69  .quest/ only    NO push run         source-gates x1, and COMPLETE
Confirmed against the runs API filtered by head_sha: only pull_request events exist for 4374c69, for every workflow, while event=push rows exist for the two earlier heads on the same branch.

So the profile was right about the mechanism and wrong about the UNIT -- it said PR where the trigger says PUSH. The original 2026-09-12 observations (PR #24 twice, PR #22 and #26 once) are all still literally true; they are just three cases where the head commit happened to agree with the cumulative diff, which is the common case and exactly why the wrong unit survived.

SECOND, SMALLER STALENESS in the same section. Its closing bullet named the required checks as "(source-gates, Tracker integrity)". Re-measured against rules/branches/main: there are THREE -- source-gates, Tracker integrity, lore check -- which is the set the ruleset paragraph at the TOP of the same profile already records, correctly, dated 2026-09-15. So one file disagreed with itself about the gate, the same defect QCLI-315 just fixed between two guide surfaces of the CLI. Worth stating plainly: the enumeration rule from QCLI-315 was written the same night and did not get applied to the file it was written in.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The profile section states the unit correctly -- the path filter applies per PUSH and the HEAD COMMIT decides whether a second source-gates row exists -- and carries the three-head measurement from PR #145 rather than asserting it
The original 2026-09-12 observations are preserved rather than rewritten, since they remain true; the amendment is additive and dated
The required-checks bullet names all three contexts, re-measured against rules/branches/main, and no longer contradicts the ruleset paragraph earlier in the same file

finalSummary:
Corrected two claims in this repository CLAUDE.md profile, both measured, both found by USING the file rather than auditing it.

1. THE UNIT WAS WRONG. The section heading said a source-touching PR fires source-gates twice. The push trigger path filter applies per PUSH, so the HEAD COMMIT decides. Measured across the three heads of PR #145: 200f203 (src/ + test/) and cbea37e (test/) each fired the push run and carried two source-gates rows; 4374c69 (.quest/ only) fired no push run at all and carried one, with mergeStateStatus already CLEAN. Confirmed against the runs API filtered by head_sha, reading the event field: only pull_request rows exist for 4374c69, for every workflow.

2. THE REQUIRED-CHECKS BULLET NAMED TWO CONTEXTS; there are three. Re-measured against rules/branches/main: source-gates, Tracker integrity, lore check, ruleset 22833771. The ruleset paragraph at the top of the same profile already had all three and was correct, so the file disagreed with itself.

The 2026-09-12 observations are preserved unrewritten -- they remain true. They were three cases where the head commit happened to agree with the cumulative diff, which is the common case and is exactly why the wrong unit survived four days without being noticed.

VERIFIED: quest agents --check --require-installed --target claude exit 0 (managed block and skill both current, untouched by the edit); lore check 63 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0.

WHY THIS COST SOMETHING RATHER THAN NOTHING. The predecessor handoff on PR #145 said, as step 1 of an ordered list, "wait for both source-gates runs". That was a faithful application of the file. Following it means waiting forever for a run that correctly never existed, on a PR that was already mergeable. A stale profile claim does not fail loudly; it turns into an instruction that stalls the next session, and the session obeying it has no reason to doubt it.

AND THE PART WORTH KEEPING. QCLI-315, closed an hour earlier in this same session, established the rule: when a fix corrects a claim, enumerate every place that claim is made and gate the enumeration. It was written about the CLI two guide surfaces contradicting each other. The required-checks bullet is the same defect -- two surfaces of ONE FILE disagreeing about the gate -- sitting in the very file the rule was recorded in, and nobody applied it there. The enumeration rule is easy to apply to the artifact under repair and easy not to apply to the instrument doing the repairing.
